record.paper: Distinct Directions and Distinct Distances in $\mathbb{R}^d$

dossier_meta.paper: Distinct Directions and Distinct Distances in $\mathbb{R}^d$
dossier_meta.statement_text: For every fixed $d$ the following holds for all $d$-norms $\|\cdot\|$ but a meagre set. For all $n>n_{0}(d)$, any set of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ that do not all lie in an affine hyperplane determine at least $(d-o(1))n$ distinct distances with respect to $\|\cdot\|$, where the $o(1)$-term tends to $0$ as $n$ tends to infinity.
dossier_meta.context_text: The conjecture concerns distinct distances in typical $d$-dimensional norms; the space of $d$-norms is a Baire space under the Hausdorff metric on unit balls, so 'all but a meagre set' is a strong genericity condition. The paper notes this is open already for $d=2$, as the result in [1] only ensures $(1-o(1))n$ distinct distances; the paper proves a weaker version (Theorem 1.6) by combining Theorem 1.2 with the arguments of [1].
